definition: Used the other player’s payoff as one’s own.
Compared payoffs for only one of the other player’s actions.
Compared cells across the other player’s actions instead of within one.
Expected the other player to pick an action that is worse for them whatever happens.
Chose an action that is not a best response to one’s own stated prediction or belief.
Called an action better whatever happens because it led to a good outcome once.
Judged a decision by its realised outcome.
Left out someone whose choice affects the outcome.
Included someone who makes no choice that affects the outcome.
Wrong account of who knows or sees what when choosing.
Misordered a player’s preferences over outcomes.
Left out an action a player can take.
Treated one’s result as depending only on one’s own choice.
Treated a tie as if one action were strictly better.
Set aside an action that is not worse in every case.
A wrong answer that matches no known misconception.
